I recently confirmed my engineering honours project with Harry Perkins Institute of Medical Research. GitHub repository.

Smart Mouse Cage Platform

Note that at this stage we are still formulating the thesis topics and project timelines. My expectation for the initial scope is prototyping a camera-based tracking system, using the existing DFK 33UX287 camera. However, we will order different parts later within a limited budget (well under $500 AUD).

Supervisors and contacts:

  1. Dr Ebrahim Vahabli
  2. Dr Shelley Waters

Description

Animal studies are an important step in testing new drugs, materials and medical devices before human studies. Monitoring animals in their cages helps researchers understand their responses to treatments and identify changes in health or behaviour. This project aims to make monitoring easier and more consistent while reducing handling and disturbance. The student will help build and test a camera-based tracking system, assemble cameras and electronics, develop software to track movement, and evaluate performance under different conditions.

  4. Real-time analysis of the behaviour of groups of mice via a depth-sensing camera and machine learning
  5. MouseVUER: video based open-source system for laboratory mouse home-cage monitoring
